text:
Alex: RFC follow-up: I pushed the slimline ownership + migration playbook draft. Need clarity on who owns the translation layer (adapter vs runtime) and the ops steps for secret rebinding during the switch. TL;DR: propose control-plane owns manifest translation; runtime owns live eviction/affinity. Thoughts?
Priya: Agree with control-plane translation but we need explicit guardrails for secret propagation. Avoid secret-rewrite during canary — that's a high blast radius.
Sam: What about tenants where private deployments use a sidecar KMS and hosted uses customer-managed keys? We need a clear fallthrough policy.
Jen: Proposed rollout sequence: 1) capability flag, 2) probe-only + metrics collection, 3) canary at 5% -> 20% -> 100%. Add runbook entries for immediate rollback.
Alex: Exactly. I added a tiny config snippet in the draft for the probe mode:
```yaml
adapter: slimline
mode: probe-only
translate_secrets: 'no-rebind'
rollout: [5, 20, 100]
```
Sam: Ops question: who wires the `no-rebind` semantic? Control-plane can mark manifests, but runtime must honor and surface failures.
Priya: Control-plane should emit the intent and validation errors. Runtime should never mutate stored customer secrets. Any rebinding must be an explicit ops action documented in the runbook.
OpsBot: deploy-bot: created canary job `slimline-rollout-v1` -> 5% traffic target. (job id: canary-2025-11-04-01)
Priya: Observability must include: token-level latency, translation_error_rate, and secret_failures per-tenant. If translation_error_rate > 0.5% for 10m we need an automated break signal.
Sam: Auto-break is ok but prefer alert-first + automated fallback to legacy adapter for a short window (2m) to avoid churn.
Jen: Agreed. Example alert expression I put in the draft: `sum(rate(adapter_translation_errors[5m])) by (tenant) / sum(rate(adapter_requests[5m])) by (tenant) > 0.005` — triggers pager + console banner.
Alex: Ownership summary so we can move forward: I (Alex) will own the control-plane translation changes and the RFC merge; Sam will own runtime fallback hooks and eviction behavior; Priya will own secret-handling policy and docs; Jen will own the runbooks and rollback checklist. Start canary next Tue unless infra flags a blocker.
Priya: Ping infra for KMS replica window and any constraints — @infra-team please advise on key rotation and read-replica sync during canary.
OpsBot: incident-bot: scheduled maintenance - KMS replica sync planned for 2025-11-10 02:00 UTC.
Sam: If infra cannot guarantee the KMS window we should pin the old adapter for 48h and schedule migration post-maintenance. That gives us a safe rollback surface.
Jen: :thumbsup: I'll draft the rollback checklist now (include steps: disable capability flag, cut traffic to legacy adapter, verify request/response parity in prod, rotate back manifests). Also UX ask: surface migration status in Console per-route (show rollout % + last error).
Alex: Good call. I'll open a Console ticket to show per-route rollout + last translation error.
Priya: One more item — load-testing thresholds. We should run a synthetic load up to 10k QPS to validate batching/caching diffs between adapters so we don't regress P95.
Sam: I'll queue the stress test and post results to /eng/runtime when done. Test will include mixed sequence lengths and cold KV-cache scenarios.
Alex: Thanks all. I'll merge the playbook draft into the repo and assign owners. If no additional blockers by EOD Friday, we mark RFC accepted and schedule the probe-only rollout. Shout here if anything changes.
Priya: Noted. Will follow up with a short doc on secret migration constraints.
Sam: Will add runtime-level telemetry hooks to the PR.
Jen: I'll publish the runbook + rollback checklist later today.
Alex: Merged. Closing thread; will post links to PRs and tickets in #eng after CI passes.
